Swapnil Tripathi

PhD Researcher · Electrical & Computer Engineering · University of California, Santa Cruz

I am a PhD student at UC Santa Cruz exploring new converter topologies, specializing in hybrid switched-capacitor converters — proposing them, designing the hardware, and testing it in the lab. The work targets high-density, high-frequency power conversion spanning kilovolt-class high-voltage buses down to 48 V, for data center, space, and aerospace applications. I completed my M.S. at IIT Madras on multilevel inverter topologies, capacitor voltage balancing, and motor drives.

Key Projects

420 W stacked-Dickson HSC prototype

800 V → 28 V GaN Hybrid Switched-Capacitor Converter

2026
PhD Research · UC Santa Cruz · Presented at PEASA 2026

A 420 W stacked-Dickson hybrid switched-capacitor stage merged with a multi-phase buck regulator at 250 kHz, built for high-voltage space and aerospace power distribution. The multilevel switch stack holds per-device stress to a fixed fraction of the bus, so 150 V GaN HEMTs run from an 800 V input, and resonant charge redistribution imposes ZVS across the Dickson stage. Measured 92.96 % peak power-stage efficiency at 128 g total mass — 3.28 kW/kg. Full hardware ownership from topology analysis through 4-layer Altium layout to bench validation.

GaN HEMT Stacked Dickson Resonant Charge Redistribution ZVS 4-Layer 2 oz Altium Space Power
50 W 48 V → 1 V prototype — symmetric dual-inductor Dickson stage, 16 switches, flying-capacitor bank on the reverse side

48 V → 1 V Switching Bus Converter — Full-ZVS RCR

2026–Present
PhD Research · UC Santa Cruz · with Abacus Power

An enhanced resonant-charge-recovery clocking scheme that pre-energizes the resonant inductor ahead of each commutation, taking the front-end 2:1 stage from the partial ZVS of prior art to complete ZVS — a control and timing contribution with no added hardware. Verified on a 50 W, 1 MHz prototype: 6-layer Altium board, symmetric dual-inductor hybrid Dickson stage, 16 switches, flying-capacitor bank on the reverse side. Efficiency improved from 86.3 % to 88.6 % at 20 A and 76.6 % to 85.4 % at 5 A.

Hybrid Dickson Full ZVS 1 MHz Point-of-Load 6-Layer Altium Data-Center Power

Grid-Tied Inverter Control

Feb–Jun 2025
Project Associate · IISc Bengaluru · Under Prof. Vishnu Mahadev Iyer

Implemented grid-tied control using a proportional-resonant (PR) controller with phase-locked loop (PLL) synchronization for a Nova converter topology. Developed real and reactive power control strategies for stable grid integration.

PR Controller PLL Nova Converter Grid-Tied

Multilevel Inverter Topologies & Motor Drives

2022–2025
M.S. Thesis Research · IIT Madras · Under Prof. Srirama Srinivas

Developed capacitor voltage balancing PWM techniques for a 10kVA cascaded H-Bridge multilevel inverter driving a 1.5kW induction motor. Implemented NPV balancing, carrier-modified PWM, and field-oriented control on a TMS320F28377S DSP + Xilinx FPGA platform. Work resulted in two published IEEE papers (ECCE & IECON 2024).

Cascaded H-Bridge TMS320F28377S FPGA FOC NPV Balancing
